text:
Lighthouses are tall structures, typically equipped with a bright light at the top to serve as a navigational aid for maritime pilots at sea or in inland waterways.
They are strategically placed on coastlines, islands, or reefs to warn ships of dangerous rocks or shallow waters and to guide them safely into harbors.
The light source, often a powerful lamp combined with a lens system like a Fresnel lens, can be seen from great distances, ensuring the safety of vessels during night or poor visibility conditions.
